assessments.reasoning: The cover identifies the Xerox PARC and SDD Version 5.0 report CSL-79-3. The introduction calls Mesa a programming system, identifies the language as one component and says the other components have separate documentation.

challenge.method: Compare the physical Version 5.0 cover and Chapter 1 against the May 1978 Version 4.0 title, the dated Alto collection, the 1976 early-users report and the later Cedar description. Check the scope of the Mesa heading in the full CHM catalog.
challenge.results: The Version 4.0 cover corroborates the naming distinction within the same Xerox publishing lineage. The Alto documentation has a different system scope, the early-users paper describes experience with an implementation, and Lampson expressly describes Cedar as derived from Mesa. The catalog groups different publications, products and implementation materials.

limitations: The bounded language referent has direct Xerox support. This identity does not assign the semantics of CSL-79-3 to earlier editions, define a product identity or establish equality with Cedar.
